overview: The churches of Lalibela illuminate the religious and architectural culture associated with King Lalibela and the Zagwe period. Builders worked downward and inward through living rock to create a sacred landscape that remains a place of worship.

items.text: Churches were carved from rock, including doors, windows, columns and roofs. Excavation and carving replaced the usual assembly of separate building blocks.
Drainage ditches, trenches and passages connected and protected the complex. Some passages opened toward caves and catacombs.
Biete Ghiorgis has a cross-shaped plan. Other churches use different layouts, and several interiors preserve mural painting.
The complex evokes Jerusalem and Bethlehem through names and sacred associations, making pilgrimage geography part of the local landscape.
Lalibela remains a center of devotion and pilgrimage. The continuation of worship extends beyond the reigns that helped establish the complex.

sources.title: UNESCO, Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela
